messages:
jonathan: Quick perf note — ran a host-path microprofile for short prompts (<=32 tokens) after the last runtime patch. Seeing a p95 regression ~18% and p99 tail widen. Flamegraph points at tokenization + request header parsing + streaming chunk assembly as ~30-45% CPU on the host side. https://perf.internal/fg/1743
maya: can you paste the profile & which transport (http1/http2/grpc)?
jonathan: HTTP/1.1 with chunked transfer for these tests. gRPC streaming was also profiled — lowers syscalls for steady streams but spikes on small-burst workloads. Test: 200 rps, batch size 1-2, KV hit ~= 60%. Profile snippet: `host:tokenize ~18%`, `parse_headers ~12%`, `chunk_assemble ~10%`, rest in networking syscalls.
sam: KV miss path still allocates per-request temp buffers and triggers full tokenizer fallback? that would explain alloc churn. Also check if we memcpy each chunk when forwarding to runtime.
maya: regex-based header parsing is probably the culprit in `parse_headers`. We used a regex for quick dev-time parse. Replace with a state-machine `strtok`-style parser or `memchr` loops. Avoid any heap allocations.
lena: short-term mitigation idea: coalesce tiny chunks server-side — wait up to N ms for more chunk data before flushing to runtime. That reduces syscall and packetization overhead at the cost of a bounded tail. Experimentally, small coalesce (8-10ms) can cut CPU by ~20% on short bursts.
jonathan: I ran a coalescing experiment: set `STREAM_COALESCE_MS=8` and enabled a buffer pool reuse path. Results: CPU down ~22%, p95 down ~18%, p99 decreased for steady load but tail +3ms on rare bursts. Gist with numbers: https://perf.internal/gist/stream-coalesce-1743
infra-bot: deploy: canary roll started for `coalesce-experiment` in staging-perf 10% -> job 4721. Logs at https://ci.internal/jobs/4721
sam: buffer reuse is low-hanging. We should maintain a thread-local buffer pool and avoid per-chunk allocations. Also try zero-copy by passing iovec directly to runtime socket if runtime API permits.
jonathan: Agreed. Also noticed kernel selection interacts here — for very short seq_len the quantized kernels incur fixed overhead that dominates. Proposal: add a small-sequence fused kernel path or prefer kernel-X for seq<=32 and batch<=4. Saves ~1.5-2ms per request.
maya: batching heuristics: switch from static max-batch to backlog-aware window. Eg dynamic window = min(8, max(1, floor(backlog/avg_enqueue_rate))). That lets tiny bursts still get coalesced into small batches without inflating latency. Also ensure we prioritize KV-cache-hit requests to avoid unnecessary cache evictions during micro-batching.
lena: I'll prototype kernel-selection toggle and a perf test that simulates tiny-prompts workload. Want unit perf harness to be part of CI (tiny-requests job).
jonathan: Action items: 1) MVP coalescing + buffer pool (jonathan/sam) 2) replace header regex with fast parser (maya) 3) kernel-selection tweak + tiny-seq perf test (lena) 4) add a microbenchmark job (tiny-requests) to CI and run against canary (everyone). I'll open PRs and link here.
lena: opened PRs: #894 (stream coalescing), #895 (buffer-pool), #896 (fast-header-parse). Links attached in PR body.
maya: will review PRs tomorrow morning. If coalescing looks good we should canary to 25% and monitor p99 & error rates. :thumbsup:
jonathan: thanks — I'll follow up with end-to-end numbers once canary hits 25%. Keep an eye on `tiny-requests` job in CI.
